newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea concerned over U.S. attacks on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea concerned over U.S. attacks on Iraq.

text.p: North Korea on Friday voiced deep concern over this week's U.S. missile attacks on Iraq, saying the military action was a violation of Baghdad's sovereignty.
"We express deep concern over the strained and unpredictable situation caused by the U.S. military action," the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said.
"The U.S. military action is a wanton violation of another country's sovereignty and territorial integrity," said the mouthpiece of communist North Korea, monitored in Tokyo.
U.S. forces fired 44 cruise missiles at air defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday in response to the Iraqi army's incursion into Kurdish areas in northern Iraq last Saturday.

"The United States describes its action as something to counter 'Iraq's violations of the U.N. Resolution.' The use of arms violating an independent state's sovereignty and territorial integrity can never be justified in any case," KCNA said.
"The situation in Iraq shows that though the Cold War is said to have come to an end, it is a worldwide inclination to settle disputes by military means," it added.
The reclusive communist state had learned from the U.S. action that it would need to prepare to counter similar attacks, KCNA said.

"The U.S. missile attack gives a serious lesson that we must be prepared at all times to counter military provocation, an outcome of the 'policy of strength,' and that we must not loosen our vigilance even a moment," it said.
"The United States must know that the 'policy of strength' is not almighty and immediately give up military action violating the sovereignty and territorial integrity of other countries," it added.
